records.title: MLDGG: Meta-Learning for Domain Generalization on Graphs
records.saved_takeaway: Graph-domain meta-learning already separates shared structure/representation parameters and domain-specific GNN parameters; tasks are source domains/graphs, and target fine-tuning is required.
records.relationship_to_candidate: No exact endpoint-positive-and-negative exclusion, persistent same-task private ensemble, or inner-only recomputed private commitment is specified. Domain/causal assumptions cannot be transferred to endpoint blocks within a single graph.

records.title: Self-supervised Auxiliary Learning for Graph Neural Networks via Meta-Learning
records.saved_takeaway: SELAR Eq. (8) and Algorithm 1 establish virtual model update, slow loss-weight meta update, then recomputed persistent model update from original weights using new loss weights. Generic recomputation ordering is direct graph prior.
records.relationship_to_candidate: Slow variable is a loss-weighting function; fast update includes shared encoder/task heads and actual commit uses the whole primary minibatch including the meta fold plus auxiliaries. No private inner-only positive-and-negative endpoint exclusion or served same-task ensemble. Algorithm outputs the trained primary network.

records.title: Graph Meta Learning via Local Subgraphs
records.saved_takeaway: Local-subgraph support/query meta-learning and single-graph disjoint-label tasks are direct graph prior. LP preprocessing splits a fixed 30% of edges to support and 70% to query; random negatives are specified without endpoint-union exclusion.
records.relationship_to_candidate: No statement excludes both endpoints of every positive and negative query from inner supervision. Inner GNN copies start from the common meta parameters; meta-testing adapts. No persistent private Adam ensemble or recomputed inner-only private commitment.

records.title: Mochi: Aligning Pre-training and Inference for Efficient Graph Foundation Models via Meta-Learning
records.saved_takeaway: Recent graph representation meta-training differentiates query loss through an episode-fitted closed-form ridge head; LP uses Hadamard edge embeddings and positive/uniform non-edge support/query samples within the same graph. No endpoint-union exclusion is stated.
records.relationship_to_candidate: Episode-fitted ridge does not supply persistent private Adam heads or ensemble commitment. H.1 describes inconsistent evaluation heads (ridge versus dot-product LP); exact inference readout is unresolved and not used for a novelty contrast.
